name: DDL database recovery for sequence objects

state_model: sequence metadata is stored as TableInfo with SequenceInfo
sequence runtime value is stored under meta sequenceKey, outside AutoIDGroup RowID/IncrementID/RandomID
DROP SEQUENCE deletes the sequence key
FLASHBACK DATABASE loads all TableInfo rows from snapshot meta and calls recoverTable uniformly
payload.severity: sequence value rollback can reuse existing application IDs after database recovery

name: Restore path must rebuild special-object runtime state

payload.description: A restore/recover path re-materializes TableInfo through a generic table path even though some object kinds have additional runtime state outside ordinary table auto IDs.
positive_signal: source object is represented by TableInfo but has kind-specific create/drop helpers
drop helper deletes side/runtime state outside the generic table row
recover path enumerates TableInfo and calls a generic create/recover helper
post-recover behavior consumes the missing side/runtime state
required_gates: direct user-visible behavior oracle, not only metadata delta
same-object normal path GREEN or sibling generic table recovery GREEN
dedup against lazy-name-resolution and prior restore reference bugs
negative_screens: ordinary create path is already permissive and only future execution fails
source deliberately disables or strips the field on recover
object recovery is blocked before publication

name: FLASHBACK DATABASE must preserve sequence next-value state

payload.p_check: FLASHBACK DATABASE enumerates historical TableInfo objects and checks schema/name/GC safety before recovering the schema.
payload.q_claim: Generic table recovery restores every object's state needed for current behavior, including sequence next-value state.
payload.failure: sequence value and cycle keys are not part of AutoIDGroup; recoverTable recreates the sequence TableInfo through CreateTableAndSetAutoID and leaves sequence value missing, so the next allocation starts from zero/start again.
side_effects: NEXTVAL returns values that already existed before the database was dropped
tables using DEFAULT NEXT VALUE FOR seq can hit duplicate primary keys after recovery
recovered application ID generators can move backward
consumers: applications using sequence values as identifiers

name: Recovered sequence must not reuse existing values

required_observations: before drop, a sequence-backed table contains rows generated from the sequence
the sequence has advanced before DROP DATABASE
FLASHBACK DATABASE restores both the table and the sequence
post-recover NEXTVAL is greater than the values already materialized, or at least cannot collide with existing rows
a default insert using the sequence succeeds without duplicate-key error
payload.red_interpretation: after FLASHBACK DATABASE, NEXTVAL returns an existing value and the next default insert fails with duplicate primary key
payload.green_interpretation: normal no-recover sequence path keeps increasing, and ordinary AUTO_INCREMENT flashback database does not reuse existing IDs
anti_oracles: only checking that FLASHBACK DATABASE succeeds
only checking existing rowset after recovery

name: FLASHBACK DATABASE with sequence-backed default table

payload.setup: database contains a sequence and a table whose primary key defaults to NEXT VALUE FOR that sequence
sequence: CREATE SEQUENCE seq START WITH 1 CACHE 100
CREATE TABLE t(id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT NEXT VALUE FOR seq, note VARCHAR(64))
INSERT two rows using defaults, producing IDs 1 and 2
SELECT NEXTVAL(seq) and then INSERT another default row
payload.expected_control: without recovery the same sequence continues to 3/4; an AUTO_INCREMENT table recovered by FLASHBACK DATABASE does not reuse 1/2
payload.expected_red: NEXTVAL(seq)=1 after flashback and the following default insert fails with duplicate key 2

name: Minimal FLASHBACK DATABASE sequence reset schedule

steps: create database, sequence, and sequence-default table
materialize at least two default-generated rows
advance the sequence once more for a clear pre-drop marker
attempt another default insert and check rowset/error
payload.stop: do not enumerate sequence option variants until the generic sequence-key restore root is fixed or owner requests blast-radius validation

title: FLASHBACK DATABASE can reset recovered sequence values and reuse existing IDs

payload.p_check: FLASHBACK DATABASE treats every historical TableInfo returned by ListTables as recoverable through recoverTable.
payload.q_claim: CreateTableAndSetAutoID restores enough runtime state for all recovered objects.
payload.fault: schema contains a sequence plus rows generated by that sequence, then DROP DATABASE and FLASHBACK DATABASE
payload.oracle: post-recover NEXTVAL must not return existing values; sequence-default insert must not hit duplicate key
controls: FLASHBACK DATABASE with AUTO_INCREMENT table preserves a non-colliding next ID
payload.validation_state: current-master RED/GREEN on authorized testbed 8220955; remote found_bug id1500003 and upstream issue 69781 confirmed

provenance.source: source proof plus testbed RED/GREEN matrix

rationale: schema recovery uses a generic TableInfo path for a special object with extra runtime state
sequence rollback is visible only through post-recover NEXTVAL/default-insert behavior
a sequence-backed primary-key default turns value reuse into a direct duplicate-key consequence
small matrix varies recovery versus no-recovery and sequence versus auto-increment

environment.front: temporary /tidb-server in fp-tidb; cleaned after run
environment.shape: FLASHBACK DATABASE containing sequence seq and table t(id DEFAULT NEXT VALUE FOR seq PRIMARY KEY)

observed: before drop, table rows were id=1 and id=2
after FLASHBACK DATABASE, table rows id=1 and id=2 were restored
following default insert failed with ERROR 1062 Duplicate entry '2' for key 't.PRIMARY'
evidence.oracle: recovered sequence must not return values already materialized in recovered table rows

lessons.quality: direct SQL-only C3 data-integrity/availability consequence; no failpoint or timing race
lessons.selector: generic restore path skipped special-object runtime-state rebuild
lessons.dedup: distinct from id30005 sequence-default lazy-name-resolution and id1500002 FK identity drift

environment.shape: same sequence-default table without DROP/FLASHBACK DATABASE

observed: two default rows produced id=1 and id=2
following default insert succeeded with id=4
evidence.oracle: sequence/default behavior is healthy without the database recovery path

lessons.quality: control proves DEFAULT NEXT VALUE FOR seq and cache behavior are not generally broken

environment.shape: FLASHBACK DATABASE containing ordinary AUTO_INCREMENT table

observed: before drop, AUTO_INCREMENT rows were id=1 and id=2
after FLASHBACK DATABASE, a default insert succeeded with id=30001
no duplicate key or ID reuse occurred
evidence.oracle: generic AutoIDGroup restoration avoids collision for ordinary tables

lessons.quality: control isolates the missing state to sequence value/cycle keys, not the whole recover schema AutoID path
